title: Spring: the refrain and the birds
work: The Four Seasons · Spring, RV 269 — I. Allegro
question: How do two recordings separate the refrain’s grouped phrases from the violin calls between them?
intro: John Harrison, Robert Turizziani and the Wichita State University Chamber Players recorded this movement live on 6 February 2000. Commons credits the other file to the Modena Chamber Orchestra, but its embedded author tag names Orpheus and its session date remains unknown. The uploader lowered that source by 20 cents without documenting the method, so neither original tuning nor original playback speed can be inferred from this file. The automatic map covers the complete 215.30- and 214.03-second files, with median confidence 0.950; use its provisional correspondence to compare phrase grouping rather than to resolve those provenance questions.

passages.label: The opening refrain
passages.note: Compare the grouping and separation of the repeated phrases. Playback levels are not a calibrated measure of the ensembles’ dynamics.

passages.label: Space between bird calls
passages.note: Follow the short violin figures and the space left between them. Do not mistake a different source pitch for different written ornament.

passages.label: The compact return
passages.note: Listen for the refrain’s second phrase rather than a complete restart; compare how the players collect the separate calls into one group.

passages.label: Pressure across the storm
passages.note: Compare the sustained drive of the rapid figures with the weight of the preceding refrain, not merely the fastest isolated note.

passages.label: A familiar return
passages.note: Follow the refrain’s grouping as the music regains E major. The matching time is approximate, not an identified bar line.

passages.label: Closing phrase and decay
passages.note: Compare the withdrawal after the final grouped phrase. Reverberation and source processing limit any inference about bow releases.
